root_cause.text: The vulnerability is a use-after-free caused by race conditions or improper synchronization allowing __xfrm_state_delete() to be called multiple times on the same xfrm_state object, where value-based predicates (x->km.seq and x->id.spi) are used to decide whether to unhash from byseq/byspi lists instead of checking actual list membership, and where bydst/bysrc deletion is unconditional, leading to double removal from hash lists that writes through LIST_POISON pointers.
root_cause.evidence: The patch description states: "__xfrm_state_delete() guards its byseq and byspi unhashes with value-based predicates: if (x->km.seq) hlist_del_rcu(&x->byseq); if (x->id.spi) hlist_del_rcu(&x->byspi); ... xfrm_alloc_spi() sets x->id.spi = newspi inside xfrm_state_lock and then immediately inserts into byspi, but a path that observes x->id.spi != 0 outside of xfrm_state_lock can still skip-or-hit the byspi unhash inconsistently with whether x is actually on the list." Additionally: "the bydst/bysrc unhashes have no predicate at all, so a second __xfrm_state_delete() on the same object writes through LIST_POISON pprev." The fix uses hlist_unhashed() and hlist_del_init_rcu() to safely handle multiple deletions.
